newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ZAGALLO INSISTS NO PROBLEM WITH ROMARIO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALLO INSISTS NO PROBLEM WITH ROMARIO.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said on Saturday that there had been no repercussions after he substituted tempestuous striker Romario during the 5-0 win over Costa Rica in the Copa America.
Romario was clearly disgruntled when he was taken off in the 75th minute and replaced by Giovanni in Friday's group C game.
Many felt the incident could lead to a rebellion by the 31-year-old Romario, who is known for his intense dislike of the substitutes' bench.
Television close-ups caught Romario uttering what appeared to be Portuguese swear words as he slunk off the field and reluctantly took his place on the bench.
"There is no problem, his behaviour has been good," Zagallo said following a training session.
"Being substituted is part of the game. I didn't like it when I was a player and it is natural he wasn't happy. The fact that he might have sworn is irrelevant."
Romario had scored a spectacular goal in the 60th minute and was clearly in the mood to show off some more of his tricks against a demoralised Costa Rican defence.
But the Romario exhibition was postponed until a later date when Zagallo decided to test one of his reserves alongside Ronaldo, Romario's striking partner.
"I wanted to carry out a test. How am I going to test another player alongside Ronaldo, for any eventuality, if I can't subsitute Romario," Zagallo said.
Romario and Zagallo have rarely been on the best of terms.
Zagallo left the striker out of the Brazil team for nearly two years following the last World Cup after being snubbed by the player.

Zagallo picked Romario for a friendly in 1995 but the player responded he did not want to play international football that year. Zagallo relented after being persuaded this year that Romario was a changed man.

The Brazilian coach was expected to have his hands full after selecting midfielder Djalminha and striker Edmundo, two other players who are known for their tantrums. They have been sent off six times between them this year in club soccer.
The world champions, hot favourites for the title, play Mexico in their second group C game on Monday.
